newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to keep open mind on new loan schemes - Hu.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to keep open mind on new loan schemes - Hu.

text.p: Singapore's finance minister Richard Hu said on Sunday the government would be monitoring new consumer credit schemes but was keen not to over-react to every innovative financial product.

Car retailers in Singapore have recently introduced new financing packages to make automobiles more attractive to buyers. In addition a bank and a real estate agency combined to offer a re-mortgaging scheme for home buyers.
"These are private arrangements and so long as they don't contravene our regulations, I think we want to avoid over regulation," Hu said in an interview on state television.
"I don't think we should over-react on every single new development, otherwise we will gain a reputation for being even more regulated than we actually are," Hu said.

Under the car financing scheme, buyers were invited to put down a large initial deposit for a luxury car, then pay a relatively small monthly installment over seven years and finish the loan with another large payment.
Hu said the government recognised that people selling things will try to come up with competitive packages.
"We will have to study these, look at how these group packages effect credit extension and so forth before we try to react to every situation."
The Monetary Authority of Singapore, of which Hu is chairman, has regularly sought to limit easy credit in the island republic to prevent private consumption growing too fast.
